feedback: Approve this single-variable test. The candidate is the iteration 5 design (score 403.4, best so far) with sensor_size changed from 0.016 to 0.012 and every other field held fixed. The change follows the rule set after iteration 5: oscillation stayed above 0.2 at kd 0.6 (oval 0.219, s-bend 0.260, slalom 0.192), so the next step is geometry, not more damping. The span stays at ±0.07 m, which iteration 4 showed removes most line loss (0.15 on the oval, 0.0 on the s-bend and slalom). Iteration 0 lost the line on every track, but it used a narrow ±0.04 m span, so that result does not show that a 0.012 m footprint causes line loss on a wide span. The candidate is valid: all sensor positions are within range, sensor_size 0.012 is an allowed option, and the weights, line_loss and observation list are allowed. Nothing is obviously broken. The main open question is whether the smaller footprint reads a sharper edge (less jitter) or loses signal at the outer sensors. Read the next race as follows. If steering_oscillation falls below 0.2 on the oval and s-bend with line_loss_events near 0, keep sensor_size 0.012 and raise base_speed in 0.1 steps (1.3, then 1.4) to test completion_time under 3 s. If line_loss_events rises above about 0.2 on any track, sensor_size 0.012 is starving the outer sensors. Return to 0.016 and test sensor y position (for example y at 0.03 m) instead. If slalom steering_oscillation rises well above 0.19, return kd to about 0.5 with kp at 2.6.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation falls below 0.2 on the oval and s-bend with line_loss_events near 0, keep sensor_size 0.012 and raise base_speed in 0.1 steps (1.3, then 1.4) with kp 2.6 and kd 0.6 fixed, to test completion_time under 3 s (iteration 1 reached progress 0.37 on the oval at base_speed 1.4).

If line_loss_events rises above about 0.2 on any track at sensor_size 0.012, return sensor_size to 0.016 and test sensor y position (for example y 0.03 m) to address the off-track endings (iteration 5 gave 0.15 line-loss events on the oval at 0.016 and 0.0 on the s-bend and slalom).

If slalom steering_oscillation rises well above its iteration 5 level of 0.192 at kd 0.6, the narrower footprint or extra damping is amplifying noise. Return kd to about 0.5 and keep kp at 2.6 (iteration 4 at kd 0.45 gave slalom oscillation of 0.102).
